title: Revelation 4 — The throne-room: 24 elders + 4 living creatures

translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — Codex Sinaiticus (א/01, 4th c. CE ~330-360) as primary uncial witness; NB Codex Vaticanus (B/03) is INCOMPLETE for Revelation. Cross-collation against Codex Alexandrinus (A/02, 5th c. CE — often the SUPERIOR Revelation witness on internal grounds), Codex Ephraemi Rescriptus (C/04, 5th c. palimpsest). P47 (Chester Beatty III, ~250 CE) preserves Rev 9:10-17:2 — does NOT preserve Rev 4. P115 lacunose for ch. 4. SBLGNT base text.

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ θύρα ἠνεῳγμένη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἡ πρώτη ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς σάλπιγγος λαλούσης μετ’ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Ἀνάβα ὧδε, καὶ δείξω σοι ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.
paragraphs.translit: Meta tauta eidon, kai idou thyra ēneōgmenē en tō ouranō, kai hē phōnē hē prōtē hēn ēkousa hōs salpingos lalousēs met’ emou legōn· Anaba hōde, kai deixō soi ha dei genesthai meta tauta.

i18n.en: After these things I looked, and behold, a door opened in heaven, and the first voice that I had heard speaking with me like a trumpet said: "Come up here, and I will show you what must take place after these things."

paragraphs.commentary: *thyra ēneōgmenē en tō ouranō* 'a door opened in heaven' + *Anaba hōde* 'come up here' marks the major narrative-transition into the throne-room vision. The throne-room established at Rev 4 is the structural framework of the remainder of the Apocalypse (Rev 4-22 takes place in or under the throne-room).

paragraphs.text: εὐθέως ἐγενόμην ἐν πνεύματι· καὶ ἰδοὺ θρόνος ἔκειτο ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον καθήμενος,
paragraphs.translit: eutheōs egenomēn en pneumati· kai idou thronos ekeito en tō ouranō, kai epi ton thronon kathēmenos,

i18n.en: At once I came to be in the Spirit, and behold, a throne stood in heaven, and one seated on the throne.

paragraphs.commentary: **MAJOR THRONE-ROOM VISION.** Cross-corpus chain: Ezek 1:26-28 (the kavod-figure on the sapphire-throne) + Dan 7:9-10 (the Ancient of Days on the fiery throne) + Hekhalot Rabbati throne-room descriptions + Shi'ur Qomah cosmic-body-of-divine tradition → Rev 4:1-11. The first NT × Hebrew Bible × Hekhalot three-way throne-vision wire in the WoH-Translation glossary. Documented at central-glossary entry `throne-vision-rev-1-4-ezek-1-dan-7-shiur-qomah-cross-corpus`. Bidirectional with existing v2.61.0 `ezekiel-1-throne-vision-merkavah-tradition-cross-corpus-hebrew-bible-hekhalot-revelation-4` and v2.59.0 `shiur-qomah-cosmic-body-of-divine-hekhalot-throne-vision-tradition`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ὅμοιος ὁράσει λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι καὶ σαρδίῳ, καὶ ἶρις κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου ὅμοιος ὁράσει σμαραγδίνῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai ho kathēmenos homoios horasei lithō iaspidi kai sardiō, kai iris kyklothen tou thronou homoios horasei smaragdinō.

i18n.en: And the one seated was in appearance like jasper and carnelian, and around the throne was a rainbow that in appearance was like an emerald.

paragraphs.commentary: *iaspidi kai sardiō* (jasper and carnelian) + *iris kyklothen tou thronou* (rainbow around the throne). The precious-stone description of the One on the throne draws on Ezek 1:26 *kĕ-marʾēh ʾeḇen sappîr* 'like the appearance of sapphire-stone' tradition and Ezek 28:13-14 high-priestly-stones tradition. The rainbow imagery directly echoes Ezek 1:28 *kĕ-marʾēh ha-qešeṯ* 'like the appearance of the bow' — the throne-vision rainbow.

paragraphs.text: καὶ κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρες, καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρας πρεσβυτέρους καθημένους περιβεβλημένους ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν στεφάνους χρυσοῦς.
paragraphs.translit: kai kyklothen tou thronou thronous eikosi tessares, kai epi tous thronous eikosi tessaras presbyterous kathēmenous peribeblēmenous en himatiois leukois, kai epi tas kephalas autōn stephanous chrysous.

i18n.en: And around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on the thrones twenty-four elders seated, clothed in white garments, and on their heads golden crowns.

paragraphs.commentary: The *eikosi tessaras presbyterous* (24 elders) — a Revelation-distinctive feature with no exact-parallel in Ezek 1 or Dan 7. Interpretive options: (i) the 24 priestly-courses (cf. 1 Chr 24:7-18); (ii) the 24 angelic-orders; (iii) the 12 patriarchs + 12 apostles symbolic-pairing; (iv) the 24 stars of the northern + southern hemispheres (some astrological-readings). The 24 elders are uniformly-clothed in white with golden crowns + thrones — emphasizing their angelic-court status as part of the throne-room council.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου ἐκπορεύονται ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί· καὶ ἑπτὰ λαμπάδες πυρὸς καιόμεναι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, ἅ εἰσιν τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα τοῦ θεοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: kai ek tou thronou ekporeuontai astrapai kai phōnai kai brontai· kai hepta lampades pyros kaiomenai enōpion tou thronou, ha eisin ta hepta pneumata tou theou,

i18n.en: And from the throne proceed lightnings and voices and thunders, and seven torches of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God,

paragraphs.commentary: *hepta lampadōn pyros kaiomenōn enōpion tou thronou* 'seven lamps of fire burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God' — the seven-spirits / seven-flame-lamps identification draws on Zech 4:2 (the seven-lamp menorah-vision) + Isa 11:2 LXX (the seven-fold spirit-listing).

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ὡς θάλασσα ὑαλίνη ὁμοία κρυστάλλῳ. Καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου τέσσαρα ζῷα γέμοντα ὀφθαλμῶν ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai enōpion tou thronou hōs thalassa hyalinē homoia krystallō. Kai en mesō tou thronou kai kyklō tou thronou tessara zōa gemonta ophthalmōn emprosthen kai opisthen·

i18n.en: and before the throne was something like a sea of glass, like crystal. And in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind.

paragraphs.commentary: **MAJOR FOUR-LIVING-CREATURES SITE.** *tessara zōa gemonta ophthalmōn emprosthen kai opisthen* 'four living creatures full of eyes front and back'. Cross-corpus chain: Ezek 1:5-25 (the four ḥayyôt with four faces and four wings) → Ezek 10 (the chayyot identified as cherubim) → Shi'ur Qomah §§45-47, 49 (the four-faces-and-four-wings amplified to 64 faces and 64 wings per creature) → Rev 4:6-8 (the NT-Christian inheritance with the four-face configuration preserved + the six-wings detail from Isa 6:2 seraphim + the singular face per zōon configuration distinct from Ezek 1). Documented at central-glossary entry `four-living-creatures-rev-4-6-8-ezek-1-chayyot-shiur-qomah-cross-corpus`. Bidirectional cross-corpus extension of the existing v2.61.0-extended `chayyot` central entry to include Rev 4 refIds.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τὸ ζῷον τὸ πρῶτον ὅμοιον λέοντι, καὶ τὸ δεύτερον ζῷον ὅμοιον μόσχῳ, καὶ τὸ τρίτον ζῷον ἔχων τὸ πρόσωπον ὡς ἀνθρώπου, καὶ τὸ τέταρτον ζῷον ὅμοιον ἀετῷ πετομένῳ.
paragraphs.translit: kai to zōon to prōton homoion leonti, kai to deuteron zōon homoion moschō, kai to triton zōon echōn to prosōpon hōs anthrōpou, kai to tetarton zōon homoion aetō petomenō.

i18n.en: And the first living creature was like a lion, and the second living creature was like an ox, and the third living creature had a face like a man's, and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle.

paragraphs.commentary: The four-face configuration (lion / ox / human / eagle) directly parallels Ezek 1:10 (with the Rev distinctive of each-creature-having-one-face rather than each-having-four). The patristic interpretation (from Irenaeus Against Heresies 3.11.8 onward) reads the four faces as symbols of the four canonical Gospels — though Irenaeus, Augustine, Jerome, and the medieval tradition distribute them differently. The patristic-iconographic interpretation is a downstream reception-tradition not constitutive of the source-text.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, ἓν καθ’ ἓν αὐτῶν ἔχων ἀνὰ πτέρυγας ἕξ, κυκλόθεν καὶ ἔσωθεν γέμουσιν ὀφθαλμῶν· καὶ ἀνάπαυσιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς λέγοντες· Ἅγιος ἅγιος ἅγιος κύριος ὁ θεός ὁ παντοκράτωρ, ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος.
paragraphs.translit: kai ta tessara zōa, hen kath’ hen autōn echōn ana pterygas hex, kyklothen kai esōthen gemousin ophthalmōn· kai anapausin ouk echousin hēmeras kai nyktos legontes· Hagios hagios hagios kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr, ho ēn kai ho ōn kai ho erchomenos.

i18n.en: And the four living creatures, each of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within; and they have no rest day and night, saying: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come."

paragraphs.commentary: **TRISAGION SITE.** *Hagios hagios hagios kyrios ho theos ho pantokratōr* — the three-fold *hagios* directly cites Isa 6:3 LXX (the seraphim's threefold-holy ascription in Isaiah's call-vision) with two modifications: (i) substitution of *ho theos ho pantokratōr* 'God the Almighty' for the LXX *sabaōth* 'of hosts'; (ii) addition of the triadic divine-name *ho ēn kai ho ōn kai ho erchomenos* 'who was and who is and who is to come' — integrating the Trisagion with the Rev 1:4 divine-name formula. The Trisagion is the foundational liturgical-formula of both the Christian Sanctus (in the Eucharistic Anaphora) and the Jewish Kedushah (in the Amidah and Yotzer-blessing). Documented at central-glossary entry `trisagion-rev-4-8-isa-6-3-sanctus-liturgical-tradition-cross-corpus`. Bidirectional with the existing Exodus entry `ehyeh-asher-ehyeh-divine-name-revelation-ex-3-14-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ὅταν δώσουσιν τὰ ζῷα δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ εὐχαριστίαν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ, τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων,
paragraphs.translit: Kai hotan dōsousin ta zōa doxan kai timēn kai eucharistian tō kathēmenō epi tō thronō, tō zōnti eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn,

i18n.en: And whenever the living creatures give glory and honor and thanks to the one seated on the throne, who lives forever and ever,

paragraphs.text: πεσοῦνται οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι ἐνώπιον τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου, καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, καὶ βαλοῦσιν τοὺς στεφάνους αὐτῶν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου λέγοντες·
paragraphs.translit: pesountai hoi eikosi tessares presbyteroi enōpion tou kathēmenou epi tou thronou, kai proskynēsousin tō zōnti eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn, kai balousin tous stephanous autōn enōpion tou thronou legontes·

i18n.en: the twenty-four elders fall down before the one seated on the throne and worship the one who lives forever and ever, and they cast their crowns before the throne, saying:

paragraphs.commentary: The 24 elders falling, worshipping, and casting their crowns. *ballousin tous stephanous autōn enōpion tou thronou* 'they cast their crowns before the throne' — the homage-gesture of the angelic-court submitting to the throne-figure. The closing doxology at v.11 establishes the Apocalypse's core theological-claim: the One on the throne is the Creator-of-all (worthiness-by-creation, distinct from the Christological-worthiness-by-redemption at Rev 5).

paragraphs.text: Ἄξιος εἶ, ὁ κύριος καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, λαβεῖν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν, ὅτι σὺ ἔκτισας τὰ πάντα, καὶ διὰ τὸ θέλημά σου ἦσαν καὶ ἐκτίσθησαν.
paragraphs.translit: Axios ei, ho kyrios kai ho theos hēmōn, labein tēn doxan kai tēn timēn kai tēn dynamin, hoti sy ektisas ta panta, kai dia to thelēma sou ēsan kai ektisthēsan.

i18n.en: "Worthy are you, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for you created all things, and by your will they existed and were created."
